sections.markdown:
## C — What white, yellow and red curbs allow, lane choice on one-way streets, white and yellow lane lines, reversible lanes, general turning rules, right on red and the left-turn paths between two-way and one-way roads
Knowledge domain: what each painted curb color lets you do, which lane to use on a long one-way street, how white and yellow lane lines differ and when they may be crossed, how reversible lanes work, the general rules for every turn, turning right on red, and how to position the car for each kind of left turn.

FACT_ID: sec13-F01 | anchor: A01
At a white painted curb you may stop only for as long as it takes to pick up or drop off passengers. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec13-F02 | anchor: A01
At a yellow painted curb you may stop only long enough to load or unload, and you must stay with your car. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec13-F03 | anchor: A01
A red painted curb means you may not stop, stand or park there at all. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec13-F04 | anchor: A01
When you will stay on a one-way street for several blocks, the center lane is usually the best lane to use. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec13-F05 | anchor: A01
On a one-way street, the left and right lanes are used by vehicles that are turning. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec13-F06 | anchor: A01
White lane lines divide lanes of traffic heading the same way. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec13-F07 | anchor: A01
A single white line may also mark the right edge of the pavement. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec13-F08 | anchor: A01
After you signal, you may cross a broken white line to change lanes if it is safe. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec13-F09 | anchor: A01
A solid white line marks the right edge of the roadway and also divides lanes of traffic heading the same way. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec13-F10 | anchor: A01
Cross the solid white edge line on the right side of the road only in an emergency or to avoid a road hazard. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec13-F11 | anchor: A01
Drivers may cross a solid white line while merging into or out of a high occupancy vehicle (HOV) lane. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec13-F12 | anchor: A01
A double solid white line divides two lanes heading the same way, and crossing it is prohibited. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec13-F13 | anchor: A01
Yellow lane lines divide lanes of traffic heading in opposite directions. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec13-F14 | anchor: A01
A single yellow line may mark the left edge of the pavement on divided highways and on one-way streets. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec13-F15 | anchor: A01
A reversible lane switches its direction of travel depending on the time of day. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec13-F16 | anchor: A01
Reversible lanes are usually marked with double dashed yellow lines. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec13-F17 | anchor: A02
Signs beside the road or overhead may tell you which reversible lanes you are allowed to use at that time. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec13-F18 | anchor: A02
Turning rules apply everywhere you turn, including driveways and alleys, not just at intersections. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec13-F19 | anchor: A02
To make any turn, signal, slow down and turn smoothly once it is safe. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec13-F20 | anchor: A02
While you turn, check for pedestrians, mopeds and bicycles. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec13-F21 | anchor: A02
Where turns may be made from more than one lane, signs and pavement markings will show you which lanes to use. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec13-F22 | anchor: A02
At some locations, signs prohibit turning. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec13-F23 | anchor: A02
Before a right turn, keep close to the right curb or road edge and do not swing wide before or during the turn. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec13-F24 | anchor: A02
To turn right at a red light, you must first come to a complete stop before the marked or unmarked crosswalk. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec13-F25 | anchor: A02
Look for No Turn On Red signs before you turn right at a red light. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec13-F26 | anchor: A02
When turning right on red, always yield to pedestrians, bicyclists and oncoming traffic. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec13-F27 | anchor: A02
Unless signs direct you otherwise, finish a right turn in the right lane of the road you enter. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec13-F28 | anchor: A02
For a left turn on a two-way road, approach in the lane just to the right of the center line and begin the turn just left of the center point of the intersection. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec13-F29 | anchor: A02
When a left turn on a two-way road is complete, you should be in the lane just to the right of the center line, which avoids conflict with other turning traffic. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec13-F30 | anchor: A02
When a left-turn lane has been signed or marked, turn left only from that lane and never from any other lane. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec13-F31 | anchor: A02
For a left turn from a one-way road onto another one-way road, approach in the lane nearest the left curb and turn into the far left lane without swinging wide. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec13-F32 | anchor: A02
Turning left from a one-way road onto another one-way road is the only left turn you may make against a red light, after stopping and yielding to traffic and pedestrians, unless signs prohibit it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec13-F33 | anchor: A02
For a left turn from a two-way road onto a one-way road, approach in the lane just to the right of the center line and turn into the far left lane of the road you enter. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec13-F34 | anchor: A02
For a left turn from a one-way road onto a two-way road, approach the intersection in the lane closest to the left curb. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0047]

Misconceptions: a white curb is for passengers, not for loading freight, and a yellow curb requires you to stay with the car; a double solid white line may never be crossed even though both sides carry traffic going the same way; the right-edge solid white line is crossed only for an emergency or a hazard; turning left against a red light is allowed only from a one-way road onto another one-way road.
Mnemonics: White curb, people in and out; yellow curb, goods in and out with you beside the car; red curb, never stop.
Glossary: reversible lane means a lane whose travel direction changes by time of day; high occupancy vehicle lane means a lane reserved for vehicles carrying more than one person, entered and left across a solid white line; swinging wide means drifting away from the curb before or during a turn.
Dynamic facts: reversible-lane schedules, posted turn prohibitions and which intersections allow turns from more than one lane are set locally and can change at any time.
